key_insight: A unified analytical and finite-element framework shows that lattice fracture toughening changes markedly above ~30% relative density, where nodal stress concentrations and crack-path geometry begin to dominate failure.
engineering_relevance: The results give designers a way to tune fracture toughness in triangular and hexagonal lattices by adjusting relative density, fillet radius, orientation, and base-material ductility for safer lightweight structures.
method: Homogenization-based analytical model coupled with blunt-crack fracture theory
Finite element simulations across low-to-high relative density lattices
Laser-cut PMMA fracture experiments for validation
evidence_signal: The model is supported by finite element results and experiments, which show a mechanism shift at high relative density and about 1.6x higher toughness in quasi-brittle PMMA lattices versus perfectly brittle ones.
watch_item: Failure becomes stochastic in brittle lattices at higher relative densities, so design predictions should account for scatter and local crack-tip geometry effects.
paper_title: Fracture of Lattice Materials from Low to High Relative Density
